verses.text: All Israel was listed by family in the Book of the Kings of Israel. Judah was taken captive to Babylon because of their disobedience.
The first to return and live on their own property in their towns were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.
People from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh settled in Jerusalem.
Among them was Uthai son of Ammihud, from the line of Omri, Imri, and Bani, a descendant of Perez son of Judah.
From the Shilonites came Asaiah the firstborn and his sons.
From Zerah's descendants came Jeuel and his relatives, six hundred and ninety in all.
From Benjamin came Sallu son of Meshullam, whose family line went back through Hodaviah and Hassenuah.
There were also Ibneiah son of Jeroham, Elah son of Uzzi and grandson of Michri, and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, whose family line went back through Reuel and Ibnijah.
Their relatives numbered nine hundred and fifty-six according to the family records. The men listed were heads of their households.
The priests included Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin.
They also included Azariah son of Hilkiah, the officer in charge of God's house. His family line went back through Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub.
There were also Adaiah son of Jeroham, from the line of Pashhur and Malchijah, and Maasai son of Adiel, from the line of Jahzerah, Meshullam, Meshillemith, and Immer.
They and their relatives who led their households numbered one thousand seven hundred and sixty. They were skilled men able to do the work of serving in God's house.
The Levites included Shemaiah son of Hasshub, whose family line went back through Azrikam and Hashabiah to Merari.
They also included Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, from the line of Zichri and Asaph.
There were also Obadiah son of Shemaiah, from the line of Galal and Jeduthun, and Berechiah son of Asa and grandson of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives. Shallum was their chief.
They had served at the King's Gate on the east side. They were the gatekeepers of the Levite camp.

Shallum was the son of Kore, whose family line went back through Ebiasaph to Korah. Shallum and his relatives, the Korahites, were responsible for guarding the entrances of the Tent. Their ancestors had guarded the entrance to the LORD's camp.
Phinehas son of Eleazar had been in charge of them in earlier times, and the LORD was with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah guarded the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
There were two hundred and twelve men chosen to guard the entrances, listed by family in their villages. David and Samuel the seer had appointed them to their trusted positions.
They and their descendants were responsible for guarding the gates of the LORD's house, the house of the Tent.
The gatekeepers stood on all four sides, to the east, west, north, and south.
Their relatives from the villages came to help them for seven days at a time.
The four chief gatekeepers were Levites in positions of trust. They were responsible for the rooms and the treasuries of God's house.
They spent the night around God's house because it was their job to guard it and open it every morning.
Some were responsible for the vessels used in worship. They counted them when they brought them in and when they took them out.
Others were responsible for the furnishings, all the vessels of the sanctuary, the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices.
Some of the priests' sons prepared the spice mixtures.
Mattithiah, a Levite and the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with the things baked in pans.
Some of their relatives from Kohath's family were responsible for preparing the bread of the Presence every Sabbath.
The singers were heads of Levite households. They lived in the rooms and were excused from other duties because their work occupied them day and night.
These were leading men among the Levites, heads of their households according to their generations. They lived in Jerusalem.
Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife was named Maacah.
His firstborn was Abdon, followed by Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, and Nadab,
then Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They also lived in Jerusalem alongside their relatives.
Ner was the father of Kish, and Kish was the father of Saul. Saul's sons were Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
Jonathan's son was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal was the father of Micah.
Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz was the father of Jarah. Jarah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza.
Moza was the father of Binea, whose line continued through Rephaiah, Eleasah, and Azel.
Azel had six sons named Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were Azel's sons.
